queries: "Minerva" "4-digit multiplication" OR "four-digit multiplication" language model fails

sources_considered.why: Shows LM accuracy on numerical reasoning tracks how often terms appear in pretraining. This fits reliance on stored patterns.
Shows a GPT-style model building an internal board-state representation. It is a possible counterexample, but the model was trained on game moves, not natural language.

receipt.public_excerpt: models are more accurate on instances whose terms are more prevalent, in some cases above $70\%$ (absolute) more accurate on the top 10\% frequent terms in comparison to the bottom 10\%.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows correct numerical answers depend heavily on how common the terms were in pretraining. That is consistent with pattern use rather than a human-like rule. It covers only some GPT-style models on numerical tasks, not 'rarely if ever' across tasks.

receipt.public_excerpt: Although the network has no a priori knowledge of the game or its rules, we uncover evidence of an emergent nonlinear internal representation of the board state.

evidence_items.explanation: A transformer sequence model formed a world-state abstraction like the one a human uses. It is a synthetic Othello model, not a natural-language LLM, so it is only context against the claim.

unresolved_gaps: No study before March 2023 measured, across tasks, how often correct LLM outputs rest on human-like or symbolic abstractions.
Interpretability of full-scale natural-language LLMs was immature at the time, so the internal basis of most correct outputs was simply unknown.
